description: A heavy torso defense constructed by riveting large overlapping iron plates inside a sturdy leather shell.  The precursor to the brigandine, common in the mid-to-late 14th century.  The exterior appears deceptively simple, but the hidden plates provide substantial protection against both cuts and thrusts.

A refined torso armor made from hundreds of small, overlapping steel plates riveted to the inside of a velvet or leather outer shell.  The evolution of the coat of plates — lighter, more flexible, and far more elegant.  The polished rivet heads form decorative patterns on the exterior, announcing the wearer's wealth and status.  A favorite of knights and wealthy men-at-arms in the late 14th to early 15th century.
